sentences.text: This large quadrupedal herbivore measured approximately 16 meters in length, similar to other sauropods.
Keith Watts first found fossils in 1974, but the type specimen QMF 7292 was not formally named until 2009 by Scott Hocknull and colleagues.
Scientists can tell Wintonotitan bones apart from Diamantinasaurus bones because the former are not as robust.
In 2009, researchers classified it as a non-titanosaurian titanosauriform sauropod.
They also suggested that Austrosaurus mckillopi is a nomen dubium differing only slightly from the holotype of Wintonotitan wattsii.
It lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago in sandstone interpreted as a river point bar.
The known remains include partial postcranial parts of the skeleton.
